newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH STOCK INVESTMENTS BALLOON IN FIRST HALF 1997.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH STOCK INVESTMENTS BALLOON IN FIRST HALF 1997.

text.p: Share prices in the Dutch stock market soared by an average 34.2 percent in the first half of this year, the second highest half year increase of the past 45 years, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said on Wednesday.
This rise was only topped in the first six months of 1983 when shares rose by 38.1 percent.
The bureau added market capitalisation had also surged.

"On June 30 this year, the value of companies on the Dutch bourse, excluding investment and property funds, reached 845 billion guilders. This is 224 billion guilders more than at the end of 1996," the CBS said.

The total return for investors, including dividends, rose by 36 percent in the first half of 1997, putting Amsterdam above the worldwide average of 31 percent, the CBS said. The Amsterdam Exchange has outperformed the world average since 1992.
The report said that Dutch high technology stocks have performed particularly well this year, rising by 62 percent.
